chief_complaint: lip swelling, hives, and wheezing after blowing up balloons
hpi_details: 35F OR nurse presents to the clinic reporting that yesterday she developed itchy hands, severe lip swelling, and wheezing within minutes of blowing up rubber balloons for her child's party. Symptoms resolved after taking Benadryl and using her husband's albuterol inhaler. She notes previously developing an itchy rash under her surgical gloves at work, and reports her mouth feels itchy when eating bananas and avocados.
ideas: thinks she has developed an allergy to the powder on the balloons
concerns: worried this will affect her ability to work as a surgical nurse
expectations: wants allergy testing and an exemption note for certain gloves at work
pmh: No chronic medical conditions. Multiple childhood surgeries for an orthopedic issue.

core_concepts: IgE-mediated latex allergy can cause localized contact urticaria to severe systemic anaphylaxis.
High-risk groups include healthcare workers and patients with multiple childhood surgeries (e.g., spina bifida).
Latex-fruit syndrome involves cross-reactivity between latex proteins and proteins in certain fruits (bananas, avocados, kiwi, chestnuts).
Diagnosis involves clinical history and specific IgE testing; management requires strict latex avoidance.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: lip swelling, hives, and wheezing after blowing up balloons

Key HPI features: 35F healthcare worker with prior glove-related contact urticaria, presenting with acute anaphylaxis symptoms after oral contact with latex (balloons). Positive history for oral allergy symptoms with bananas/avocados.
Objective/Exam findings: Vitals stable today. Exam is unremarkable as symptoms have resolved, but history is classic for anaphylaxis.
Relevant background/PMH: Multiple childhood surgeries, OR Nurse
common_misconceptions: Confusing irritant contact dermatitis or allergic contact dermatitis (Type IV) with true IgE-mediated (Type I) latex allergy.
Failing to recognize the connection between fruit allergies (banana, avocado) and latex.
Underestimating the risk of airborne anaphylaxis in high-latex environments.
dangerous_errors: Failing to provide an Epinephrine auto-injector to a patient with a history of latex-induced airway symptoms.
Allowing the patient to continue using latex products in the workplace, risking a fatal occupational exposure.
management_principles: Strict avoidance of all natural rubber latex products (gloves, balloons, condoms, certain medical supplies).
Prescribe Epinephrine auto-injectors (2-pack) and instruct on use.
Occupational health referral for latex-safe workplace accommodations.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Latex-fruit syndrome cross-reactivity does not always guarantee systemic anaphylaxis to the foods, but they should be avoided if they cause symptoms.

reference_soap.subjective: 35F OR nurse presents with a history of acute lip swelling, urticaria, and wheezing after blowing up balloons, resolving with antihistamines and albuterol. Reports prior hand pruritus with surgical gloves and oral pruritus with bananas/avocados.
reference_soap.objective: Patient is asymptomatic today. Vitals stable. Chest is clear. No active skin lesions.
reference_soap.assessment: IgE-mediated Latex Allergy with prior anaphylactic reaction and suspected Latex-Fruit syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Strict avoidance of all natural rubber latex products. 2. Prescribed Epinephrine auto-injector (0.3mg) 2-pack; counselled on indications and technique. 3. Refer to Allergy/Immunology for serum specific IgE testing (ImmunoCAP) for latex. 4. Provide a letter for Occupational Health requesting a strict latex-free environment. 5. Avoid bananas and avocados, which cause oral symptoms; assess other potentially cross-reactive foods based on symptoms. 6. Obtain medical alert identification.

learning_objectives: Identify risk factors for latex allergy, including healthcare occupation and multiple past surgeries
Recognize Latex-Fruit syndrome (cross-reactivity with bananas, avocados, kiwi, chestnuts)
Institute preventative management including strict avoidance and Epinephrine auto-injector prescription

teaching.one_liner: An IgE-mediated allergy to natural rubber latex common in healthcare workers, frequently cross-reacting with specific fruits like bananas and avocados.
differentials: Type IV Allergic contact dermatitis (to glove chemicals/accelerators)
red_flags: Respiratory symptoms (wheezing, throat tightness) upon exposure, indicating systemic anaphylaxis risk rather than just local dermatitis.

must_ask.objective: Identify occupational and past surgical risk factors
must_ask.say: Do you work in healthcare or have you had multiple surgeries in the past?
Do you get an itchy mouth or throat when eating bananas, avocados, or kiwis?
Did you have any trouble breathing, coughing, or wheezing during the reaction?

history.answer: Yesterday, my lips swelled up and I started wheezing right after blowing up balloons for my child's birthday party.
It came on suddenly within ten minutes of blowing up rubber balloons yesterday afternoon, and it lasted about an hour until the medication kicked in.
It was scary; I felt very tight in my chest and struggled to catch my breath even while sitting down.
The wheezing happened suddenly after the balloons, but today my breathing feels completely back to normal.
No, I have never had sudden wheezing or trouble breathing like this before.
No, I didn't have any problem lying flat, and I didn't wake up gasping for air at night.
It started right while I was blowing up rubber balloons; cold air, exercise, and dust have never bothered my breathing.
Yes, my chest was whistling with a distinct high-pitched wheeze when I breathed out.
No, I have not had a cough, phlegm, or any fever.
My lips puffed up huge within minutes, and my hands and arms broke out in itchy red hives.
No, I didn't have any crushing or sharp chest pain, just difficulty moving air in and out.
My heart was racing because I was frightened, but I did not feel faint or dizzy.
No, I haven't coughed up any blood.
No, I haven't noticed any swelling in my feet or legs, and my weight has been steady.
No, neither leg is swollen or tender, and I haven't been on any long trips or stuck in bed.
No, I don't feel unusually fatigued or pale, and I have not had any unusual bleeding.
I was very anxious because I couldn't breathe, but I didn't have any tingling or numbness around my mouth or fingers.
No, I have never been diagnosed with asthma, chronic bronchitis, or any heart condition.
I took a dose of Benadryl and used two puffs of my husband's albuterol inhaler, which eased the wheezing within thirty minutes.
Now that you mention it, my lips and mouth get itchy and tingle whenever I eat fresh bananas or avocados.
Yes, I frequently get an itchy, red rash on my hands after wearing surgical gloves during long procedures at work.
I wonder if I might have developed an allergy to the powder coating on the balloons.
I am very worried that this might be an allergy that could jeopardize my job as an operating room nurse.
I hope to get proper allergy testing and an official note recommending latex-free gloves for my hospital unit.
I have no chronic medical conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
I had multiple orthopedic surgeries on my legs during childhood, but no surgeries as an adult.
I do not take any daily prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to penicillin or any other medications.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I only drink one glass of wine on occasional weekends, nothing heavy.
I work full-time as an operating room nurse, and I live at home with my husband and young child.
No one in my immediate family has asthma, severe allergies, or early heart disease.
My last menstrual period was two weeks ago and completely normal; I have an intrauterine device and cannot be pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-appearing, alert, and in no acute distress, with no accessory muscle use or cyanosis.
Lips and tongue appear normal without swelling; posterior pharynx is clear with no uvular edema.
Jugular venous pressure is normal with no visible neck vein engorgement.
Resonant to percussion across all lung fields bilaterally.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally with good air entry and no wheezing, rhonchi, or crackles.
Normal S1 and S2 with a regular rhythm, and no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
No pitting edema noted in either lower extremity.
Both calves are symmetric, soft, and non-tender, with no warmth or cord-like induration.
No active urticaria, wheals, or facial swelling; hands show mild dryness but no acute dermatitis.
